notes: An adverb used to express inability or impossibility. It's placed directly before the verb. It's different from 안 (an), which expresses a lack of will or simple negation. '못 가다' means 'cannot go' (due to circumstances), while '안 가다' means 'to not go' (by choice).
--- word ---
term: 갔는데
type: Verb Ending
breakdown: 가다 + -았- + -는데
meaning: I went, but...
notes: A connective ending used to provide background information or context for the following clause. It can mean 'but,' 'and,' or 'so,' depending on the context. Here, it creates a soft contrast and leaves the sentence hanging, inviting the next thought.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V + -는데 / A + -(으)ㄴ데
meaning: A connective ending that provides background information for the next clause. It can indicate a soft contrast ('but'), a reason ('so'), or simply set the scene ('and').
example: 비가 오는데 우리 영화 볼까? (It's raining, so shall we watch a movie?)
level: Beginner

=== [45:39] 해변을 못 간 게 좀 아쉽지만 ===
meaning: It's a bit of a shame that I couldn't go to the beach, but...
tone: Informal, expressing slight regret, transitional.
--- word ---
term: 해변을
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 해변 + 을
meaning: the beach
notes: 해변 (haebyeon) means 'beach.' The particle -을 is the object marker, indicating that the beach is the object of the action (of going).
--- word ---
term: 못
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: cannot
notes: This adverb indicates inability. '못 가다' means 'to be unable to go.' It's distinct from '안 가다', which means 'to not go' by choice.
--- word ---
term: 간
type: Verb (Modifier Form)
breakdown: 가다 + -ㄴ
meaning: that (I) went
notes: This is the past-tense noun-modifying form of the verb 가다 (to go). It turns the verb into an adjective that can describe a noun. For example, '내가 간 곳' (naega gan got) means 'the place that I went.'
--- word ---
term: 게
type: Noun (Contraction)
breakdown: 것 + 이
meaning: the fact that / the thing that
notes: 게 (ge) is a very common colloquial contraction of 것이 (geos-i), which is '것' (thing/fact) plus the subject particle '이'. The whole phrase '해변을 못 간 게' means 'the fact that I couldn't go to the beach.'
--- word ---
term: 좀
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: a little, a bit
notes: A common adverb used to soften a statement or indicate a small degree. It makes the sentence sound more natural and less blunt. It's a contraction of 조금 (jogeum).
--- word ---
term: 아쉽지만
type: Adjective Ending
breakdown: 아쉽다 + -지만
meaning: it's a shame, but...
notes: 아쉽다 (aswipda) is an adjective describing a feeling of regret, sadness over something lacking, or a near miss. The ending -지만 means 'but' or 'although,' connecting this clause to the next one with a contrast.
--- grammar ---
pattern: Verb + -(으)ㄴ 것
meaning: A grammar pattern used to turn a past-action verb clause into a noun phrase. It means 'the act of having done (verb)' or 'the fact that (verb) happened'. The colloquial form is -(으)ㄴ 게.
example: 어제 영화 본 것이 재미있었어요. (The movie I watched yesterday was fun.)
level: Beginner

=== [45:42] 내 나름대로 그래도 내가 좋아하는 화성을 갔다 왔으니까 ===
meaning: Still, in my own way, I went to Mars, which I like, so...
tone: Informal, self-reassuring, explanatory.
--- word ---
term: 내
type: Pronoun
breakdown: 
meaning: my
notes: The informal possessive pronoun for 'I'. It's a contraction of 나의 (na-ui). The formal equivalent is 저의 (jeo-ui).
--- word ---
term: 나름대로
type: Adverb
breakdown: 나름 + 대로
meaning: in my own way
notes: This expression means 'in one's own way' or 'according to one's own style/judgment.' It implies a personal, unique approach to something. For example, '나름대로 열심히 했어' (nareumdaero yeolsimhi haesseo) means 'I worked hard in my own way.'
--- word ---
term: 그래도
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: still, nevertheless
notes: An adverb used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or exists in spite of what was previously said. It's similar to 'but still' or 'even so'.
--- word ---
term: 내가
type: Pronoun + Particle
breakdown: 나 + 가
meaning: I (as the subject)
notes: The informal pronoun 나 (I) combined with the subject marker 가 (ga). This explicitly marks 'I' as the one performing the action of 'liking'.
--- word ---
term: 좋아하는
type: Verb (Modifier Form)
breakdown: 좋아하다 + -는
meaning: that (I) like
notes: The present-tense noun-modifying form of 좋아하다 (to like). It acts like an adjective describing the following noun, '화성' (Mars). So, '내가 좋아하는 화성' means 'Mars, which I like.'
--- word ---
term: 화성을
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 화성 + 을
meaning: Mars
notes: 화성 (Hwaseong) means 'Mars'. The story bible indicates Hwasa uses this as a nickname for Joshua Tree National Park. -을 is the object particle.
--- word ---
term: 갔다 왔으니까
type: Verb Ending
breakdown: 갔다 오다 + -았- + -(으)니까
meaning: because I went and came back
notes: 갔다 오다 is a compound verb meaning 'to go and come back.' The ending -(으)니까 indicates the reason or cause for the next statement. It often implies the speaker's personal judgment or experience is the basis for the reason.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V/A + -(으)니까
meaning: A connective ending that expresses a reason or cause. It's often used when the following clause is a suggestion, command, or a statement of the speaker's realization. It translates to 'because' or 'since'.
example: 날씨가 좋으니까 공원에 가자. (Since the weather is nice, let's go to the park.)
level: Beginner

=== [45:48] 나는 거길 그냥 화성이라고 불러 ===
meaning: I just call that place Mars.
tone: Informal, declarative, explaining a personal nickname.
--- word ---
term: 나는
type: Pronoun + Particle
breakdown: 나 + 는
meaning: As for me, I
notes: The informal pronoun 나 (I) with the topic marker 는 (neun). Using the topic marker here emphasizes 'I' (as opposed to others) and sets the topic of the sentence.
--- word ---
term: 거길
type: Adverb (Contraction)
breakdown: 거기 + 를
meaning: that place
notes: A colloquial contraction of 거기를 (geogi-reul). 거기 means 'there' or 'that place,' and -를 is the object marker.
--- word ---
term: 그냥
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: just, simply
notes: A very common adverb that can mean 'just' or 'for no particular reason.' Here, it implies she calls it Mars without a deep, complex reason, it's just what she does.
--- word ---
term: 화성이라고
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 화성 + -이라고
meaning: as 'Mars'
notes: The particle -(이)라고 is used for quoting nouns. It attaches to the noun being quoted or named. The full pattern is 'Noun + (이)라고 부르다' (to call something 'Noun').
--- word ---
term: 불러
type: Verb
breakdown: 부르다
meaning: call
notes: The informal, non-polite present tense conjugation of 부르다 (to call). The base form 부르다 is an irregular '르' verb; when conjugated, it becomes 불러 (bulleo).
--- grammar ---
pattern: Noun + (이)라고 부르다
meaning: The pattern for saying 'to call (someone/something) [Noun]'. If the noun ends in a vowel, use -라고. If it ends in a consonant, use -이라고.
example: 사람들은 저를 '화사'라고 불러요. (People call me 'Hwasa'.)
level: Beginner

--- grammar ---
pattern: V + -(으)ㄹ 때
meaning: A grammar pattern that means 'when...' or 'at the time of...' It attaches the future noun-modifying ending -(으)ㄹ to a verb stem, followed by 때 (time).

=== [46:01] 저녁이 된... 한 노을 질 때쯤 이렇게 보면 진짜 화성이야 막 이렇게... ===
meaning: When it becomes evening... around sunset, if you look at it like this, it's really Mars, just like...
tone: Informal, descriptive, trailing off.
--- word ---
term: 저녁이
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 저녁 (evening) + 이 (subject particle)
meaning: evening (as the subject)
notes: The particle 이 marks '저녁' (evening) as the subject of the verb '되다' (to become). In casual speech, subject particles are sometimes omitted, but here it clarifies what is becoming.
--- word ---
term: 된...
type: Verb
breakdown: 되다 (to become) + -(으)ㄴ (past adjective modifier)
meaning: which became...
notes: This modifies a noun that is implied but unstated (e.g., 'the time that became evening'). The -(으)ㄴ ending turns a verb into a descriptive clause that happened in the past. The '...' indicates she is pausing or trailing off.
--- word ---
term: 한
type: Determiner
breakdown: 
meaning: about, around
notes: Used before numbers, counters, or time-related nouns to mean 'approximately'. It's different from 한 as the number 'one' (from 하나).
--- word ---
term: 노을
type: Noun
breakdown: 
meaning: sunset, sunset glow
notes: Refers specifically to the reddish glow in the sky during sunrise or sunset, not just the event of the sun setting.
--- word ---
term: 질
type: Verb
breakdown: 지다 (to set/fall) + -(으)ㄹ (future adjective modifier)
meaning: that will set
notes: Here, '지다' is used in the set phrase '노을이 지다' (the sun sets). The -(으)ㄹ ending modifies the following noun '때' (time), creating the meaning 'the time when the sun will set'.
--- word ---
term: 때쯤
type: Noun + Suffix
breakdown: 때 (time) + 쯤 (around)
meaning: around the time
notes: 쯤 is a suffix attached to nouns of time, quantity, or place to mean 'about' or 'approximately'. It's very common in everyday speech.
--- word ---
term: 이렇게
type: Adverb
breakdown: 이렇다 (to be like this) + -게 (adverbial ending)
meaning: like this, in this way
notes: A very common adverb used to demonstrate something or to refer to a manner of action that is clear from context. It's the adverbial form of the adjective 이렇다.
--- word ---
term: 보면
type: Verb
breakdown: 보다 (to see/look) + -(으)면 (if/when)
meaning: if you look
notes: The -(으)면 ending expresses a condition ('if') or a time ('when'). Here, it means 'when you look' or 'if you look'.
--- word ---
term: 진짜
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: really, for real
notes: A very common colloquial adverb used for emphasis, similar to 'really', 'seriously', or 'totally' in English. It can be used more frequently in speech than its English equivalents might suggest.
--- word ---
term: 화성이야
type: Noun + Copula
breakdown: 화성 (Mars) + -이야 (informal copula 'to be')
meaning: it's Mars
notes: This is the informal, non-polite (반말) form of '화성이다' (it is Mars). The -이야 ending is used after a noun ending in a consonant. If the noun ends in a vowel, -야 is used (e.g., '사과야' - it's an apple).
--- word ---
term: 막
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: just, like
notes: A colloquial filler word that adds emphasis or a sense of spontaneity. It can mean 'recklessly', 'intensely', or just be used as a conversational tic, similar to 'like' or 'just' in English. Its meaning is highly context-dependent.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-(으)ㄹ 때쯤
meaning: Indicates 'around the time when' something happens. It combines the future modifier -(으)ㄹ with 때 (time) and the suffix 쯤 (around).
example: 수업이 끝날 때쯤 전화해. (Call me around the time class ends.)
level: Beginner
--- grammar ---
pattern: Noun + -(이)야
meaning: The informal, non-polite (반말) form of the copula 이다 (to be). Used among close friends or to people younger than the speaker. -이야 is used after consonants, -야 after vowels.
example: 이건 내 책이야. (This is my book.)
level: Beginner

notes: 나 (na) is the informal word for 'I/me'. The pattern '나만의' (namanui) specifically means 'my very own', emphasizing that it's personal and unique to her. She corrects herself from '언니만의' to the more direct '나만의'.
--- word ---
term: 우주야
type: Noun + Copula
breakdown: 우주 + -야
meaning: it's a universe
notes: 우주 (uju) means 'universe' or 'space'. -야 (-ya) is the informal, non-polite ending for the verb 'to be' (이다) when attached to a noun ending in a vowel. If the noun ends in a consonant, -이야 (-iya) is used.

--- word ---
term: 와

meaning: I come back
notes: The informal, non-polite (반말) form of 와요. The entire phrase '충전이 돼서 와' is an idiomatic way to say 'I come back recharged' or 'it's so refreshing'.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-아/어서
meaning: Indicates a sequence of actions ('do V and then...') or a reason ('because of V...'). It connects two related clauses.
example: 배가 고파서 밥을 먹었어요. (I was hungry, so I ate.)
level: Beginner

meaning: Indicates trying or experiencing an action. It adds a nuance of 'giving something a shot'.

level: Beginner
--- grammar ---
pattern: V + ~고 싶다
meaning: Expresses the speaker's desire or wish to do something.
example: 영화 보고 싶어. (I want to watch a movie.)
level: Beginner

=== [50:21] 근데 그게 있다더라 발리에서 조심해야 될 것들이 있다고 하더라? ===
meaning: But I heard there are things you have to be careful about in Bali?
tone: Informal, conversational, seeking confirmation.
--- word ---
term: 근데
type: Adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: But, by the way
notes: A very common contraction of '그런데' (geureonde). Used in casual speech to mean 'but' or to change the topic, similar to 'anyway' or 'by the way'.
--- word ---
term: 그게
type: Pronoun + Particle
breakdown: 그거 + 가
meaning: That thing
notes: A contraction of '그것이' (geugeos-i) or '그거가' (geugeo-ga). '그거' refers to 'that thing' (already mentioned or known), and '가' is the subject particle. This contracted form is standard in spoken Korean.
--- word ---
term: 있다더라
type: Verb
breakdown: 있다 + -다더라
meaning: I heard there is/are
notes: The '-다더라' ending is used to report something you heard from someone else. It's a casual, conversational form. '있다' means 'to exist' or 'to have'.
--- word ---
term: 발리에서
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 발리 + -에서
meaning: in Bali
notes: The particle '-에서' marks a location where an action takes place. It's often translated as 'in', 'at', or 'from'.
--- word ---
term: 조심해야
type: Verb
breakdown: 조심하다 + -아야/어야 하다
meaning: have to be careful
notes: Part of the '조심해야 될 것' phrase. '조심하다' means 'to be careful'. The '-아야/어야 하다' pattern expresses obligation or necessity, meaning 'must' or 'have to'.
--- word ---
term: 될
type: Verb Modifier
breakdown: 되다 + -ㄹ
meaning: that will be / that should be
notes: This is the future adnominal form of '되다' (to become). Here, it works with '조심해야' to modify '것들', creating the meaning 'things that one must be careful of'.
--- word ---
term: 것들이
type: Noun + Particle
breakdown: 것 + -들 + -이
meaning: things
notes: '것' means 'thing'. '-들' is the plural marker. '-이' is the subject particle used after a consonant. The full phrase '조심해야 될 것들' means 'things one must be careful of'.
--- word ---
term: 있다고
type: Verb
breakdown: 있다 + -다고
meaning: that there is/are
notes: The '-다고' ending is part of an indirect quotation, used here with '하더라' to mean '(I heard) that there are...'. It reports a statement.
--- word ---
term: 하더라?
type: Verb
breakdown: 하다 + -더라
meaning: I heard?
notes: '-더라' is a retrospective ending, used when recalling something one saw, felt, or heard. Combined with a question mark, it seeks confirmation for something the speaker recalls hearing. It's like saying, 'I heard that..., is that right?'
--- grammar ---
pattern: -다더라 / -라더라
meaning: Used to report something you heard from another person. It's a casual, spoken form.
example: 그 식당이 맛있다고 하더라. (I heard that restaurant is delicious.)
level: Intermediate
--- grammar ---
pattern: -아야/어야 하다/되다
meaning: Expresses obligation or necessity, equivalent to 'must' or 'have to'.
example: 숙제를 해야 해요. (I have to do my homework.)
level: Beginner

meaning: As for me
notes: 나 (na) is the informal pronoun for 'I', used with friends or people younger than you. The formal equivalent is 저 (jeo). The topic marker 는 (neun) indicates what the sentence is about, and can sometimes add a nuance of contrast.
--- word ---
term: 몰랐었어
type: verb
breakdown: 모르다 (to not know) + ~았었~ (double past tense) + ~어 (informal ending)
meaning: I didn't know (at that time)
notes: The double past tense marker ~았/었었~ emphasizes that a past state is completely over and has no connection to the present. While the simple past 몰랐어 (mollasseo) is more common, 몰랐었어 adds a nuance of 'I had no idea back then, but now I do'.
--- grammar ---
pattern: ~았/었었~ (Double Past Tense)
meaning: Used to emphasize a completed action or state in the more distant past that is no longer relevant to the present. It can be translated as 'had done' or 'used to do'.
example: 어렸을 때 여기 살았었어요. (I used to live here when I was young.)
level: Intermediate

--- word ---
term: 것도
type: noun + particle
breakdown: 것 + 도
meaning: the act of... also
notes: 것 (geot) is a dependent noun meaning 'thing' or 'act'. Here, 관리하는 것 means 'the act of managing'. The particle 도 (do) means 'also' or 'too'.
--- word ---
term: 귀찮고
type: adjective
breakdown: 귀찮다 + -고
meaning: is bothersome and...
notes: 귀찮다 (gwichanta) means 'to be a hassle' or 'bothersome'. The -고 (-go) ending connects clauses, meaning 'and'. The sentence trails off, implying she has more to say on the topic.
--- grammar ---
pattern: V + -는 것
meaning: Turns a verb into a noun phrase, meaning 'the act of V-ing' or 'the thing that one V-s'.
example: 매일 운동하는 것은 어려워요. (Exercising every day is difficult.)
level: Beginner

=== [51:19] 이 호텔이 와도 상수도가 안 좋대? ===
meaning: They say the water supply is bad even at this hotel?
tone: Informal, questioning, repeating a fan's comment.
--- word ---
term: 이
type: determiner
breakdown: 
meaning: this
notes: 이 (i) is used before a noun to mean 'this', referring to something close to the speaker. Compare with 그 (geu, 'that') and 저 (jeo, 'that over there').
--- word ---

type: noun + particle
breakdown: 호텔 + 이
meaning: this hotel (subject)

--- word ---
term: 와도
type: verb
breakdown: 오다 + -아도
meaning: even if one comes
notes: The verb 오다 (oda) means 'to come'. The grammar pattern -아/어도 (-ado/-eodo) means 'even if' or 'although'. Here, it's likely part of a phrase from a fan's comment she's reading.

term: 상수도가
type: noun + particle
breakdown: 상수도 + 가
meaning: the water supply (subject)

--- word ---
term: 안
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: not
notes: A short-form negator placed directly before a verb or adjective. It's more common in spoken Korean than the long-form negation -지 않다 (-ji anta).

meaning: is it said to be good?

=== [51:29] 내가 뒤집어져 버리면 ===

term: 내가
type: pronoun + particle
breakdown: 내 + 가
meaning: I (subject)

breakdown: 뒤집어지다 + -어

meaning: if (it) completely...
notes: This combines two grammar points. -아/어 버리다 (-a/eo beorida) is an auxiliary verb that adds nuance of completion, finality, or sometimes regret. -면 (-myeon) is a conditional ending meaning 'if'. Together, it means 'if X happens (completely/unfortunately)...'
--- grammar ---
pattern: -아/어 버리다
meaning: An auxiliary verb construction that emphasizes the completion of an action, often with a sense of relief, finality, or regret.

meaning: if it's a heatwave
notes: The sentence ends here, implying the rest is to follow. This is common in spoken Korean, where thoughts are broken into smaller chunks. '폭염' (pok-yeom) means 'scorching heat' or 'heatwave'.
--- grammar ---
pattern: Noun + -(이)면
meaning: A conditional pattern meaning 'if it is [Noun]'. It's used to set up a hypothetical situation based on the noun. '이면' is used after a noun ending in a consonant, and '면' is used after a noun ending in a vowel.
example: 학생이면 할인받을 수 있어요. (If you're a student, you can get a discount.)

=== [1:00:10] 더워 죽을 것 까지야 ===
meaning: It's to the point where I could die from the heat.

term: 더워
type: Adjective
breakdown: 덥다
meaning: being hot
notes: This is the conjugated form of '덥다' (to be hot). It's a 'ㅂ' irregular verb, so when conjugated with '-어/아', the 'ㅂ' changes to '우' and combines with '어' to become '워' (더우 + 어 -> 더워).

notes: This combines the past tense -었- (eot) with the speculative ending -나 봐 (na bwa). This ending is used to express a guess or assumption based on some evidence or feeling. It's very common in casual speech.
--- grammar ---

meaning: Used to express a speaker's supposition or guess based on an observed fact or situation. It translates to 'it seems/looks like' or 'I guess'. -나 보다 is used with verbs and 있다/없다, while -(으)ㄴ가 보다 is for adjectives.

--- word ---
term: 이렇게
type: adverb
breakdown: 
meaning: like this, in this way
notes: A demonstrative adverb. It's part of a set: 이렇게 (ireoke - like this), 그렇게 (geureoke - like that, near the listener), 저렇게 (jeoreoke - like that, over there).

type: verb phrase
breakdown: 하다 + -ㄴ 거 + -이었- + -는데
meaning: it was something I did, but...
notes: A complex but common colloquial form. It breaks down into: 한 거 (colloquial for 한 것, 'the thing that was done') + -이었- (past tense of 이다, 'to be') + -는데 (connective ending providing background). The whole phrase sets up a context or contrast for what comes next.

example: 그는 의사라고 했어요. (geuneun uisarago haesseoyo.) - He said he is a doctor.

--- grammar ---

--- grammar ---

meaning: When I was young (as for that time)

notes: Here, '허용' (heoyong) is used with the object particle '-을' because it is the object of the verb '하다' (to do). The phrase '허용을 하다' means 'to permit' or 'to allow'.

meaning: Expresses a strong feeling of being unable or unwilling to do something, often due to an internal feeling or judgment rather than a physical limitation.

=== [1:26:24] 새로웠어 ===
meaning: it was new/refreshing.

term: 새로웠어
type: Adjective
breakdown: 새롭다 + -었어
meaning: was new
notes: This is the informal past tense of 새롭다 (to be new/fresh). It's a 'ㅂ' irregular verb. When conjugating with a vowel ending, the 'ㅂ' changes to '우', so 새롭 + -었어 becomes 새로워 + -었어 -> 새로웠어.
--- grammar ---

meaning: Verbs/adjectives ending in 'ㅂ' (like 춥다, 덥다, 새롭다) change the 'ㅂ' to '오' or '우' when followed by a vowel.

notes: 몰입 (morip) means 'immersion' or 'deep concentration'. The particle '이' marks it as the subject of the verb '되다' (to become). The phrase '몰입이 되다' means 'to become immersed'.
--- word ---
term: 되는
type: Verb
breakdown: 되다 + -는
meaning: that becomes / that is
notes: This is the verb '되다' (to become) modified by the '-는' ending, which turns it into a present-tense adjective. It modifies an implied noun, like '느낌' (feeling). The full phrase would be '몰입이 덜 되는 느낌' (a feeling of being less immersed).
--- grammar ---
pattern: V-는 (Noun)
meaning: Present-tense adjective modifier. Turns a verb into an adjective that describes a noun.
example: 지금 읽는 책 (The book I am reading now)
level: Beginner
